about: Say It Again, Dexter uses two panels from Dexter's Laboratory. In the top one, the boy genius Dexter, with his red hair, big glasses and white lab coat, is squeezed between two swooning girls, one cupping his face and the other leaning in for a kiss. In the close-up below, Dexter leans in, mouth open, whispering into the blonde girl's ear while she smiles with her eyes closed and a little heart floats nearby. The meme frames any phrase as so irresistible that it needs to be whispered a second time.
origin: The scene comes from "The Big Cheese", an episode in the first season of Dexter's Laboratory on Cartoon Network that aired in 1996. Dexter is stuck saying nothing but "omelette du fromage", in a thick French accent, and the girls ask him to say it again.
usage:
Put the same phrase in both boxes: the top one is the line that impresses, the bottom one is Dexter whispering it again for effect. Repetition is the joke, so changing the second line breaks the format; at most, make it a bit more intimate.

The funniest choices are nerdy or mundane phrases treated as seductive: technical jargon, a sports stat, a food order, a tax term, a gaming phrase. Lowercase or all caps both work, as long as the phrase is short enough to read twice.
ideas: your order is ready for pickup
your order is ready for pickup
aka: I Love Your Accent, Say It Again
